h1: How Decathlon turned customer behavior into business decisions
sub: Decathlon relied on Flame Analytics to better understand how visitors interacted with its stores and use that information to optimize the shopping experience, improve operations and support data-driven decision-making.

quote.text: Understanding how customers behave inside the store makes it possible to make better decisions about space, operations and the shopping experience.
quote.author: Retail Operations team

elCaso: Decathlon, one of the world's largest sporting goods retailers, wanted to add a more complete view of customer behavior in its physical stores.
Beyond sales, the company needed to understand how visitors interacted with the retail space, which areas saw the most activity and how to optimize the shopping experience with objective data.
To do so, Decathlon deployed Flame Analytics as its retail intelligence platform, adding continuous information on customer behavior to support the day-to-day management of its stores.

blocks.h2: Understanding everything that happens before the purchase

body.p: Sales show the final outcome of commercial activity, but they do not explain how customers behave during their visit.
Decathlon needed to answer key questions to improve the management of its stores:

list: How many visitors does each store receive?
How do traffic flows evolve throughout the day?
Which areas concentrate the most activity?
How long do customers stay in the store?
How can product distribution be optimized?
How can the allocation of in-store resources be improved?
How can this data be used to improve the shopping experience?

body.p: The goal was to add a layer of intelligence that would turn visitor behavior into a tool to optimize operations and improve business performance.

blocks.h2: A complete view of in-store behavior

body.p: Flame Analytics deployed a platform able to measure and analyze visitor activity inside the store through traffic, dwell-time and behavior indicators.

Thanks to this data, Decathlon could learn how customers used the retail space, identify the areas with the most activity and assess the impact of changes in product distribution or commercial campaigns.
The information was presented through intuitive dashboards that made it possible to analyze the evolution of each store and support decision-making with objective data.

body.h3: Data to optimize the shopping experience

body.p: The analytics generated by Flame helped improve key aspects of daily operations, such as the organization of the retail space, resource planning or the evaluation of marketing initiatives.
This information enabled more efficient point-of-sale management and allowed the experience to be continuously adapted to customers' real needs.
With Flame Analytics, Decathlon had continuous information on the activity of its stores.
Teams could analyze footfall patterns, study visitor journeys, identify improvement opportunities and assess the impact of the changes made at the point of sale.
This data helped support decisions related to:

body.h3: From customer behavior to continuous improvement

body.p: The project marked another step in Decathlon's strategy to manage its stores through objective information.
Having indicators on visitor behavior made it possible to better understand how retail spaces worked and to apply continuous improvements based on real data.

Thanks to Flame Analytics, the company turned the daily activity of its stores into useful knowledge to optimize operations, strengthen the shopping experience and improve the performance of its retail network.
